description: Create a workflow, or replace the one with this name (saving the same definition again changes nothing more). A workflow is a reusable run definition: start it with create_run and its name, or on a timetable with create_schedule. Connections must already be saved in the organization; reference them by name, never with a URL or a credential. Read the current definition with get_workflow first when you change part of it, because saving replaces the whole definition. Give it a description, and an input_schema and output_schema (JSON Schemas) so that agents can discover and call it: a run's input is checked against input_schema before it starts, and its output must be JSON matching output_schema or the run fails.

allowed_methods.description: HTTP methods allowed, for example ["GET"] for read-only access.

allowed_tools.description: Tool names allowed on an MCP connection.

ref.description: Name of the saved connection (see list_connections).

connections.description: Saved connections the agent may use (at most 16), keyed by the name the agent sees. Each refers to a connection saved in the organization and can only narrow it.

description.description: What the workflow does and what input it expects, in a sentence or two, for people and agents. At most 500 characters.

files.description: Files placed in the sandbox (at most 32): inline content, or a file saved in the organization.

file.description: Id of a saved file (see list_files), instead of content.

path.description: Where the file appears in the sandbox, a relative path.

input_schema.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 or 7, at most 32 KiB, no references to other documents) that each run of this workflow's input must match. A run whose input does not match is refused with the path and the reason, such as "input.city: required".

model.description: A model id from list_models. Omit for the default.

name.description: The workflow's name: letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores.

output_schema.description: A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12 or 7, at most 32 KiB, no references to other documents) that each run of this workflow's output must match. The agent is told the schema and asked to reply with JSON only; the output is then checked, and a run whose output does not match fails with the reason.

prompt.description: What the agent should do (maximum 128 KiB).

shell.description: Whether the agent may run shell commands in its sandbox.

web.description: Web access: true, false, or an object limiting it.

allow.description: Domains the agent may fetch, such as "api.github.com" or "*.example.com". Empty allows every public domain.

search.description: Whether web search is available (default true).

zero_data_retention.description: Record nothing of the runs' content; the output is kept only briefly and released on first retrieval.

name: save_workflow
title: Save a workflow
